highConfidenceFindings.stemPattern: before a maximal exercise test, the practitioner should first verify:
highConfidenceFindings.correctOptionPattern: Screening, contraindications, preparation, and emergency procedures
distractorPattern: Confirm history, medication, and symptoms without reviewing emergency readiness
Rely on previous scores and coach expectations instead of screening
Assume experienced staff and precise equipment remove contraindications
highConfidenceFindings.rationale: After the stem's verify: the keyed noun phrase completes the sentence grammatically, while every distractor begins with a bare verb and does not. The answer can therefore be selected from syntax rather than content.
highConfidenceFindings.recommendedAction: Rewrite all four options as parallel noun phrases or as complete clauses. Preserve the safety concept and key, but remove the unique grammatical form of the correct option.

highConfidenceFindings.stemPattern: a test administrator should stop an exercise test when:
highConfidenceFindings.correctOptionPattern: Predefined termination criteria or concerning symptoms occur
distractorPattern: Stop only after a maximal score has been reached
Continue if the athlete wishes even after a warning sign
Stop at a fixed time regardless of symptoms or protocol
highConfidenceFindings.rationale: After when: the keyed option is the only complete finite clause. All distractors begin with imperative-style verbs, so the correct answer is exposed by grammar before the safety principle is considered.
highConfidenceFindings.recommendedAction: Rewrite all four options as parallel finite clauses, for example by giving each option an explicit subject and verb. Preserve the termination-criteria answer.
